the Tertiary rocks are more differentiated than the Quaternary rocks.
the Tertiary rocks of the Adak and Kanega areas are characterized by high concentrations of alkalis, iron, titanium, and manganese, and low concentrations of magnesium, calcium, and phosphorus.

the Tertiary rocks from Adak are of a basaltic composition, whereas the Quaternary rocks are of a trachytic composition; the rocks from Kanaga show a similar change, except that in the case of Kanaga, a younger cone of trachytic composition has grown within the older shield of basaltic composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rocks from the three centers on Adak and the shield volcano on Kanaga Island are all similar and are probably related genetically to one another.
